purpose: Estrogen is most commonly used to relieve symptoms of menopause, such as hot flashes, night sweats, and vaginal dryness. It can also be used to prevent bone loss (osteoporosis) after menopause. In some cases, it is used as part of hormone therapy for transgender women or to treat certain hormone-related conditions.
how_it_works: Estrogen is a natural hormone your body makes, mainly in your ovaries. When estrogen levels drop — like during menopause — you can get uncomfortable symptoms. This medication replaces or supplements the estrogen your body is no longer making enough of, helping to bring your hormone levels back to a more comfortable balance and relieving those symptoms.
common_side_effects: Breast tenderness or swelling, nausea, headaches, bloating, mood changes, vaginal spotting or light bleeding (especially when first starting), and skin irritation if using a patch or gel.
warnings: Estrogen can increase the risk of blood clots, stroke, heart attack, and certain types of cancer (such as breast and uterine cancer) in some people, especially with long-term use. Tell your doctor if you have a history of blood clots, heart disease, stroke, liver problems, or certain cancers. Do not smoke while using estrogen — it greatly raises your risk of serious side effects. Always use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time needed.
typical_dosing: Dosing depends on the form and reason for use. Pills are often taken once daily. Patches are usually changed once or twice a week. Creams, gels, or sprays are applied to the skin daily. Vaginal rings are inserted and replaced every 3 months. Your doctor will find the right dose and form that works best for you.
